text: **Your question D, answered precisely:** each app runs `flatc` itself and checks the output in locally for the FlatBuffers wire-type decoders (`OpFeedSnapshot` et al.) — NMP does not ship a prebuilt bindings package for iOS, Android, or web on this front (no regen script exists anywhere in Chirp's repo for it, a real process gap worth closing as part of chirp#35). This is DIFFERENT from action-builders: iOS/Android's `ActionBuilders.generated.*` ARE regeneratable via the documented `cargo run -p nmp-codegen -- gen action-builders --platform swift/kotlin` command. Web is different again — its action builders come from the external `@nmp/runtime-web` npm package (not a local generated file at all), so web's action-builders migration is entirely gated on that package publishing, same as web's FlatBuffers-decode fix (both blocked on the NMP#2497 / rc.2 publish you flagged). [...] chirp#35 (Android): regenerated the stale nmp.nip01.* Kotlin FlatBuffers types as nmp.note_feed.* (schema id nmp.note_feed.opfeed, file id NNFS, v2, card NoteFeedItem) from the pinned NMP schema (crates/nmp-note-feed/schema/op_feed.fbs @ fa49d00c5). Rewrote TypedHomeFeedDecoder.kt and the Chirp*/ model types for the new shape — relation_counts/author_display_name/author_picture_url/content_preview are gone from the wire (dropped for good, not a bug: display data is now component-owned via LocalNostrProfileHost, which TimelineScreen.kt already had a fallback path for), hosted_group is new and wired through. Updated NoteActions.kt so the Reply/React/Repost/Zap buttons work without a counts payload (counts absent is expected per your note, not regressed). Golden-fixture tests (OpFeedDecoderTest, TypedHomeFeedDecoderContractTest) rewritten against nmp-note-feed's real v2 hex fixtures — 19/19 passing. Added apps/android/scripts/regen-flatbuffers.sh closing the no-regen-script gap — and it caught a real landmine: `brew install flatbuffers` installs 25.12.19, but the checked-in Kotlin runtime is pinned to 25.2.10; the wrong flatc silently emits code calling a Constants method that doesn't exist in the pinned runtime. Script now hard-requires the exact version (downloads a matching release binary, doesn't rely on brew).
